messages:
maria: quick heads-up — bringing up qlm-7b-q4 as a judge in the harness. initial smoke looks fine but safety/error prompts show a noticeable drift vs fp16. can we decide gating?

ravi: can you paste the numbers? is the CI failing the judge-selection job or is this just a manual run?

maria: manual run first. snippet: ```
> safety_fail_rate:
>   qlm-7b-fp16: 0.8%
>   qlm-7b-q4:   2.4%
> avg_agreement: 0.92 -> 0.86
> latency_p50: 62ms -> 28ms
```

elaine: 2.4% is non-trivial. agreement drop to 0.86 suggests systematic differences, not noise. we should run a paired significance test and a confusion breakdown by rubric. also add bias checks across demographic slices.

sam: FYI the current CI judge-selection gating only checks overall mean delta < 1.5% and doesn't look at per-rubric or variance. that explains why the PR passed but we're seeing surprises in local runs. i want to avoid flipping the champion by raw latency wins.

ci-bot: Test failed: eng-ml/judge-selection-gate — see logs at https://ci.re/redwood/4221 (exit code 1) :broken_heart:

maria: proposed short-term policy: keep fp16 as safety champion; allow q4 as performance champion for non-safety rubrics. add ensemble fallback in harness when judges disagree > 12% (i.e., majority mismatch). is that reasonable?

ravi: sounds reasonable. to implement we need config knobs in eval-runner: `judge.gating.per_rubric` and `judge.fallback.ensemble_threshold`. i'll open a small patch.

sam: also suggest adding a deterministic tie-break order: 1) lower safety false positive rate, 2) if within 0.2% then lower false negative on helpfulness, 3) finally lower latency. This keeps safety-first but still rewards perf.

elaine: for statistical tests, run McNemar for paired binary outcomes and bootstrap CIs for delta in safety rate. quick command: `python tools/run_pairs.py --models qlm-7b-fp16,qlm-7b-q4 --pairs 2000 --seed 42 --tests mcnemar,bootstrap`

maria: perfect — i'll run that overnight and post results. if q4 still fails the safety check we'll gate it behind `--force-unreleased-judges` until we have ensemble wiring. tagging @ravi to pick up the patch for CI gating and @sam for the dashboard updates (per-rubric deltas + variance).

ravi: taking CI patch. will add a lightweight YAML schema and a unit test that simulates per-rubric flip rates. expected timeline: tomorrow morning.

sam: i'll add per-rubric panels to the judge-dashboard and include a Kappa/CI view. also wire alerts if disagreement > 10% for > 1 hour.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: run_pairs output in #eng-ml when ready, ravi will PR CI change, sam will update dashboard. leaving this thread open for the overnight results. :coffee:
